notes: Official sites textbooksonline.tn.nic.in and textbookcorp.tn.gov.in could not be read: WebFetch was refused by their robots.txt, and the shell has no internet access. dge.tn.gov.in and tnschools.gov.in were not reached either. The chapter and section titles were therefore taken from copies of the official SCERT/Government of Tamil Nadu textbook PDFs hosted on cdn1.byjus.com (and, for Grade 11 Vol I, on 11thstudymaterials.wordpress.com). These are mirrors of the government PDF (cover 'GOVERNMENT OF TAMIL NADU', '(c) SCERT', 'A publication under Free Textbook Programme') and were used only because the official host was unreachable.

Section titles are the top-level numbered sections from each volume's contents page, as reported by the fetch tool. Capitalisation follows the printed contents, which is inconsistent in the book itself. The fetched PDF text had OCR/ligature artefacts (e.g. 'Th eorem'), so small punctuation or capitalisation differences are possible. Sub-sections (e.g. 1.2.1) are omitted because they could not be seen for every chapter.

Edition for 2026-27: the books in use are still the 'Published under New Syllabus' set (first edition 2018 for Std XI, 2019 for Std XII, with later revised editions). News reports (DT Next, updated 16 Aug 2026; Madhyamam, 6 Nov 2025) say new textbooks under the Tamil Nadu State Education Policy 2025 are being prepared for 2027-28. I found no sign that new Std XI or XII mathematics books were issued for 2026-27. Annual reprints may carry a later reprint year that I could not see.

Reduced syllabus: TN cut the syllabus for the COVID-affected years (2020-21 onward). I found no reduced-syllabus or deleted-portions notice for 2026-27 from DGE or SCERT. Secondary syllabus listings (shaalaa.com, careers360) show the full 12-chapter syllabus for 2026-27. This could not be confirmed on dge.tn.gov.in.

Business Mathematics and Statistics (Std XI and XII, 2 volumes each) is a separate Higher Secondary subject taken in commerce streams. It shares some chapter names (e.g. 'Applications of Matrices and Determinants') but is not inventoried here. Only the Mathematics (core) textbook is covered.
Outcomes are written in my own words from the section structure. They are not official TN learning outcomes: I found no separate official learning-outcomes document for Higher Secondary mathematics.
The existing competencies were written to NCERT grade bands. Some TN placements differ, and mappings follow the skill, not the grade label.

Std XI public examination: a Government Order under SEP 2025 (reported 13 Oct 2025) cancelled the Class XI public examination from 2025-26. Std XI is now assessed by the school, but the textbook and syllabus are unchanged.
Section 8.7 is printed 'Direction cosines and directon ratios' (sic) in the contents and is recorded as printed.
Section 3.9 'Inverse trigonometric functions' in Std XI is an introduction. The full treatment is Std XII Chapter 4.

Unlike NCERT, TN Std XI covers matrices and determinants, vectors (incl. dot and cross product), limits and continuity, the full differentiation toolkit, indefinite integration, and conditional probability with Bayes' theorem. Existing NCERT Grade 12 competencies were mapped where the skill matches.
The Std XI chapter list matches between the 2018 first edition and the 2019/2020 revised edition. Changes inside chapters (examples, exercises) were not compared.

sections.title: 1.4 Constants and variables, intervals and neighbourhoods

outcomes.statement: Perform set operations, use Venn diagrams and count elements of unions with the inclusion-exclusion idea.
Form Cartesian products and write relations between sets as sets of ordered pairs, finding domain and range.
Decide whether a relation is reflexive, symmetric, transitive or an equivalence relation, and find equivalence classes.
Write sets of real numbers using interval notation and describe neighbourhoods of a point.

competencies.why: Writing sets of real numbers in interval notation is apintch (and interval operations apintop); neighbourhoods of a point are the new family aenbhd.

outcomes.statement: Identify functions, find their domain and range, and classify them as one-one, onto or bijective.
Compose functions and find the inverse of a bijective function.

competencies.why: Composition of functions (evaluating f∘g and finding the composite of two functions) is assessed by these families of the function-operations competency, which the outcome is not mapped to.

outcomes.statement: Sketch graphs of standard functions such as modulus, signum, step and polynomial functions and transform them by reflection, translation and dilation.

proposed.name: Graph functions using translations, reflections and dilations
proposed.why: Existing algebra.functions covers domain, range and function types; no competency covers transforming a known graph (y=f(x)+c, f(x+c), -f(x), f(-x), af(x), f(ax)).

sections.title: 2.10 Application of algebra in real life

outcomes.statement: Use properties of real numbers and absolute value to solve equations and inequalities involving modulus.

proposed.name: Solve equations and inequalities involving absolute value
proposed.why: No existing competency covers |x| as distance, or solving |ax+b|=c and |ax+b|<c type problems.

outcomes.statement: Solve linear inequalities in one variable and graph linear inequalities in two variables.
Analyse quadratic functions: roots, nature of roots, graph, and form equations whose roots are related to given roots.

competencies.why: Forming the quadratic whose roots are α + k, kα or α² from a given quadratic is the family apvform (Vieta relations); the outcome is mapped only to the discriminant and quadratic-solving competencies.

outcomes.statement: Solve quadratic and rational inequalities by sign analysis.

proposed.name: Solve quadratic and rational inequalities
proposed.why: algebra.inequalities is limited to linear inequalities; sign-analysis of quadratic and rational expressions is a separate skill.

outcomes.statement: Divide polynomials and use the division algorithm, remainder and factor theorems.
Resolve rational functions into partial fractions with linear and quadratic factors.

proposed.name: Decompose rational functions into partial fractions
proposed.why: No existing competency covers partial-fraction decomposition; it is also a prerequisite for integrating rational functions.

outcomes.statement: Simplify expressions with rational exponents and radicals, including rationalising.
Apply the laws of logarithms, change bases and solve logarithmic and simple exponential equations.

proposed.name: Use logarithm laws and solve logarithmic equations
proposed.why: The list has exponent laws but no competency for logarithms (definition, change of base, laws, log equations).

outcomes.statement: Convert between degree and radian measure and use arc length and sector area in radians.
Evaluate trigonometric functions of any angle using quadrants, allied angles, periodicity and odd/even properties.
Prove and apply compound, multiple, sub-multiple angle and sum-to-product identities, including conditional identities.

competencies.why: Applying compound, multiple and sub-multiple angle formulas is assessed in the compound-angle-identities competency (exact values of A ± B, double angles, product-to-sum, half angles, simplifying with the sum formulas); the outcome is mapped only to trigonometric functions and identities, which have

outcomes.statement: Find principal and general solutions of trigonometric equations.
Use the sine rule, cosine rule, projection formula, half-angle formulae and area formulae for a triangle.

proposed.name: Solve triangles using sine, cosine and projection rules
proposed.why: trigonometry.ratios is right-triangle only and heights-distances is applied right-triangle work; sine rule, cosine rule, projection formula and half-angle formulae for general triangles are absent.

outcomes.statement: Solve triangles and applied problems (e.g. distances and heights) using the properties of triangles.

proposed.name: Solve triangles using sine, cosine and projection rules
proposed.why: trigonometry.ratios is right-triangle only and heights-distances is applied right-triangle work; sine rule, cosine rule, projection formula and half-angle formulae for general triangles are absent.

outcomes.statement: Describe inverse trigonometric functions with restricted domains and evaluate principal values.
Count outcomes using the addition and multiplication principles and simplify factorial expressions.
Count arrangements, including with repetition, restrictions, identical objects and circular arrangements, and find rank of a word.
Count selections using combinations and apply properties of nCr in geometric and practical counting problems.
Prove summation, divisibility and inequality statements using the principle of mathematical induction.

proposed.name: Prove statements by mathematical induction
proposed.why: reasoning.mathematical-argument and proof-intro are generic; the principle of mathematical induction is a distinct proof technique not covered.

outcomes.statement: Expand binomials with positive integer index and find a general term, middle term or a specified coefficient.
Find terms and sums of arithmetic and geometric progressions in context.
Work with arithmetico-geometric and harmonic progressions and relate arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means.

proposed.name: Work with arithmetico-geometric and harmonic progressions
proposed.why: Existing sequence competencies cover only AP and GP; AGP terms/sums and HP (and AM-GM-HM relations) are not covered.

outcomes.statement: Evaluate finite series using standard sums of powers of natural numbers and telescoping.

proposed.name: Sum finite series using standard sums and telescoping
proposed.why: No existing competency covers sigma notation sums such as sum of n, n^2, n^3 or telescoping (method of differences).

outcomes.statement: Find sums of infinite geometric and arithmetico-geometric series and recognise convergence.

proposed.name: Work with arithmetico-geometric and harmonic progressions
proposed.why: Existing sequence competencies cover only AP and GP; AGP terms/sums and HP (and AM-GM-HM relations) are not covered.

outcomes.statement: Use binomial series for any rational index, and exponential and logarithmic series, for expansions and approximations.

proposed.name: Use binomial, exponential and logarithmic series
proposed.why: algebra.binomial is for positive integer index; series for (1+x)^n with rational n, e^x and log(1+x), and approximations from them, are not covered.

outcomes.statement: Find the equation of the locus of a point moving under a given geometric condition.

proposed.name: Derive the equation of a locus
proposed.why: No existing coordinate competency covers translating a geometric condition on a moving point into an equation.

outcomes.statement: Write the equation of a line in slope-intercept, point-slope, two-point, intercept, normal and parametric forms and convert between them.
Find the angle between lines, test for parallel or perpendicular lines, and compute distance from a point to a line and between parallel lines.
Use families of lines, including lines through the intersection of two given lines, and the position of a point relative to a line.
Identify when a second-degree equation represents a pair of lines, find the separate lines, the angle between them and their angle bisectors.

proposed.name: Analyse pairs of straight lines from second-degree equations
proposed.why: coordinate.straight-lines covers single lines; homogeneous/general second-degree equations representing two lines, the angle between them and angle bisectors are absent.

outcomes.statement: Classify matrices by type and perform addition, scalar multiplication, multiplication and transpose.

competencies.why: As for tn-g10-c03-o08: the transpose is assessed in the transpose-symmetry competency, which this outcome is not mapped to; classifying matrices by type is now apmtype.

outcomes.statement: Express a square matrix as the sum of symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices and use their properties.
Evaluate determinants using expansion and properties, including factorisation of determinants.
Use determinants to find area of a triangle and test collinearity, and compute products of determinants.

competencies.why: Area of a triangle and collinearity from vertices (determinant formula) already exist there; products of determinants are in audt3.

sections.title: 8.3 Representation of a vector and types of vectors

outcomes.statement: Distinguish scalars and vectors, identify types of vectors and add or scale vectors geometrically and algebraically.
Use position vectors and the section formula to locate points dividing segments internally or externally.
Resolve vectors into components and find unit vectors, direction cosines and direction ratios.

competencies.why: atdc asks for the direction cosines of the vector joining two points (the unit vector's components, from direction ratios); the outcome is mapped only to space-coordinates and vectors.algebra.

outcomes.statement: Compute scalar and vector products and use them for angles, projections, perpendicularity and areas.
Estimate limits from tables and graphs and use one-sided limits to decide whether a limit exists.
Evaluate limits using limit laws, factorisation, rationalisation and standard limits involving trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions.
Evaluate limits at infinity and identify infinite limits.
Test functions for continuity at a point and on an interval and classify discontinuities.

chapters.title: Differential Calculus - Differentiability and Methods of Differentiation

outcomes.statement: Find derivatives from first principles and interpret the derivative as slope of a tangent and as instantaneous velocity.
Test differentiability using one-sided derivatives and relate it to continuity.
Differentiate elementary functions using sum, product, quotient and chain rules.
Differentiate implicit, parametric and logarithmically-differentiable functions, inverse trigonometric functions, and one function with respect to another.

competencies.why: Implicit, parametric and logarithmic differentiation already exist in that competency; inverse trigonometric derivatives and 'with respect to another function' are the new family audinv.

outcomes.statement: Compute higher-order derivatives and verify differential relations.

sections.title: 11.4 Integrals of the form f(ax + b)

outcomes.statement: Find antiderivatives of standard functions, including functions of the form f(ax + b), using basic rules.
Use an antiderivative with an initial condition to solve simple applied problems such as recovering position from velocity.
Integrate by decomposition, partial fractions and substitution.

proposed.name: Decompose rational functions into partial fractions
proposed.why: No existing competency covers partial-fraction decomposition; it is also a prerequisite for integrating rational functions.

outcomes.statement: Integrate by parts, including Bernoulli's formula for repeated integration by parts.
Integrate rational and irrational forms reducible to standard integrals such as 1/(a^2 +/- x^2) and sqrt(a^2 - x^2).
Describe random experiments, sample spaces and types of events, using tree diagrams and tables.
Compute probabilities using classical and axiomatic definitions and counting methods.
Apply addition theorems and complement rules to combined events.
Compute conditional probabilities, use the multiplication rule and test independence of events.

competencies.why: Testing independence (P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B)) is already asked by atindt and used by atindu, in a competency the outcome is not mapped to.

outcomes.statement: Apply the total probability theorem and Bayes' theorem to infer causes from observed outcomes.
